public_rationale: On January 9, 2023, Wolfram compared unaided ChatGPT’s mathematical answers with computational results and showed plausible but incorrect answers [e1]. This supports the contextual claim that contemporary unaided ChatGPT was not a dependable substitute for precise numerical computation [e1].
limitations: The demonstration provides no representative mathematical error rate and does not establish an impossibility applying to all future language models or systems using computational tools [e1].

The January 31, 2023 evaluation’s supplied abstract does not establish when responses were collected, so it cannot establish performance during the November 30, 2022–January 14, 2023 target period [e2].
The November 30, 2022 launch disclosure acknowledges incorrect answers but does not measure mathematical accuracy [e3].

from_speaker: Statistical word prediction is no substitute for real math
our_interpretation: In the surrounding discussion of a pace calculation, the ordinary reading is that contemporary unaided ChatGPT was not a dependable replacement for mathematical computation requiring correct numerical answers.
This is not interpreted as a theorem that all future language models must fail at mathematics, or that contemporary models could solve no mathematical problems.
For this ongoing observation, use the publicly observable period from ChatGPT’s launch through the post, November 30, 2022 to January 14, 2023.
The supplied normalized proposition concerns mathematical substitutability; the accompanying assertion about how many people believed otherwise is not separately quantified.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporary demonstrations show plausible but wrong mathematical results from unaided ChatGPT on tasks handled correctly by direct computation.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Contemporary evaluations establish dependable replacement of direct computation across the relevant numerical tasks, and the alleged failures are shown to be misreported or outside that scope.
